parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by the luminosity of a star.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how a standard candle in a distant galaxy can be used to determine the distance of the galaxy from an observer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The Sun has a radius of $6.96 \times 10^8 \text{m}$ and a surface temperature of $5780 \text{K}$. Light from the Sun is observed to have a peak intensity at a wavelength of $501 \text{nm}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the luminosity of the Sun. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Another star emits radiation that has a peak intensity at a wavelength of $624 \text{nm}$.

Determine the surface temperature of this star.
